parsed.explanation: Rated on the documented combined regime. Same-sex conduct is criminalised (up to one year, applies to women) with low documented enforcement, but the dossier records arrests of LGBTQ people after attackers invoked their status, deterrence of victim reporting, and state-level rhetorical defence of the laws. An active legislative threat (harsh bill, proposed imprisonment of children from age 10) has an unresolved status. Gender-affirming care is absent domestically, a real exposure for a visitor with medical needs. No trans-specific border, document, facility or custody rule is documented; visitor entry and detention practice is not documented. Violence data is absent. Employment protection exists but enforcement is undocumented. Overall: elevated risk, driven by a state-supported climate and the care gap rather than by a documented universal-exposure measure.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry, document-marker or screening rule is documented for visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Any document-mismatch risk cannot be assessed from the record; it is not documented as operating.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Some LGBTQ people have been arrested on the basis of sexuality or gender identity after attacks; the sodomy statute is a potential police lever, though enforcement is described as uncommon.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Enforcement is described as uncommon; no documented custody-placement rule for trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest after victimisation can place a visitor in custody; custody practice for trans people is not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access or bathroom restriction is documented. The record is national with no subnational variation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No parent-local interaction is documented; the national statute is the operative rule.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming hormone therapy and surgery are documented as unavailable domestically, so a visitor cannot obtain transition-related care there. Emergency-care treatment of trans patients is not documented.
care_services.interaction: Care denial interacts with travel: a visitor who needs continuity of hormones has no local route.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The president defended the criminalising laws in 2012. Anti-gay sentiment is documented, and a legislator seeks support for a harsh bill targeting homosexuality, including child imprisonment proposals.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No documented official protection for trans people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level framing of gay conduct as a threat raises the social license for hostility toward gender-nonconforming visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Proposals would imprison children as young as 10 for gay sex. Status is unresolved, and no trans-specific minor rule is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's exposure depends on whether the proposals pass; a guardian bears the risk of any custody event.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Concealment is the documented norm. Attackers have used LGBTQ status as an excuse, and reporting is deterred. No trans-specific violence rate with a denominator is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: A small number of advocacy-sponsored private spaces exist.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victimisation followed by a deterred police report leaves the visitor without recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The 2015 labour non-discrimination provision has no documented enforcement. The 2013 HIV figure is dated and covers MSM only; the 2020 UN report is the latest structured assessment.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Section 2.4(b)(iii) of the 2015 labour statute is in force on paper, with no documented operation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse for a visitor is largely untested; legislative outcomes are unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a documented universal exclusion register with near-absent appeals. This dossier documents no comparable universal-exposure measure, so it sits above 0.35-A. Its criminal statute is low-enforcement, and that gap is the main reason it is higher.

0.45-B documents enforced care restrictions and education exclusion. This dossier documents care unavailability but no enforced exclusion from services, and its criminal-law exposure is less active. It is therefore similar in tier, with slightly less documented enforcement.

0.55-C documents ward-placement friction and partial care denial with functioning remedies. This dossier has no documented placement rule and no working remedy, but it adds a criminal statute, arrests after victimisation, and a hostile state climate, so it sits below 0.55-C.

parsed.synthesis: The documented exposures are a low-enforcement criminal statute that still produces arrests after victimisation, deterred reporting, and an active legislative threat with child-imprisonment proposals. A state-level rhetorical defence of the laws adds hostility. Domestic unavailability of gender-affirming care is a concrete gap for a visitor with medical needs. Protections are a labour-law clause with no documented enforcement and a few advocacy-sponsored spaces. No universal facility, document or border measure is documented, and no trans-specific violence rate exists. Because the outcomes of the legislative bill are unresolved and the most recent structured report is from 2020, the rating is held in the elevated band rather than lower.
